correctness.rationale: The Rayleigh minimum on the orthogonal complement of constants is concave even when the rate support is disconnected, so averaging over price-preserving rotations, reflection and layer swap suffices for the global value without imposing symmetry on feasible inputs. Fourier modes on the cycle and the two layer parities give sigma(a+c) and sigma a+(4−sigma)c+2b. Their minimum after discarding only the constant mode is the stated three-mode gap. Scaling to gap one gives three half-spaces plus nonnegativity. The all-positive three-active point has a=c=U/2 and negative b, and the zero-coordinate faces give exactly A,C,M1,M2 and, when delta>0, D. In particular beta+delta=4 implies U−z−1/4=beta(U−1/2)/(beta−delta)>0, so the two b=0 junctions are in the required order. The objective is strictly positive on nonzero recession rays; the minimizing face is the convex hull of its minimum-cost vertices. The factor n in the total cost follows from 2n rails, n rungs and 2n diagonals. For s>1, M2 dominates C,M1 and (when present) D, leaving A versus M2; for s<1 the candidates A,M2 are dominated, and the difference J_D−J_M1 has the sign of s−delta/beta. Comparing C to the resulting no-rung candidate gives the stated thresholds, including the three-way odd crossover and s=1 segment. Traversing only forward crossed edges reverses layer each step, giving one 2n-cycle for odd n and two n-cycles for even n.
residual_risks: Floating-point boundary comparisons are supplemental; the analytic cost comparison proves exact equality. In the frozen verifier phase_checks counts grid visits, including some points at which conditional assertions are skipped; it is not 640 separate strict-equivalence assertions.
The optimizer classification applies only to rates constant within each of the three priced classes; nothing here excludes additional nonsymmetric global optimizers.
